Commentary.Commentary: The umpires are out on the field. The fielding team has taken their respective positions. Rahmanullah Gurbaz and Riaz Hassan, the opening batters for Afghanistan walk out to bat. Shaheen Afridi has the new ball in his hand and is raring to go. Let's go...
... THE RUN CHASE ...

Right then, Pakistan will be the happier of the two sides at the halfway mark. They are on course here to dish out a 3-0 hammering to Afghanistan. On the other hand, Afghanistan could not finish well with the ball and now need to bat out of their skins to avoid a whitewash. Can Rahmanullah Gurbaz repeat his heroics from the last game? We shall find out when we return in a bit for the chase.

As far as Afghanistan are concerned, the new ball pairing of Fazalhaq Farooqi and Mujeeb Ur Rahman set the tone for them and did not allow Pakistan to get off to a flying start. Coming in for his first game of the series, Gulbadin Naib was switched on from ball one and got rid of the two Pakistan openers in quick succession. In the middle overs, Rashid Khan, Fareed Ahmad, and Mohammad Nabi kept things quiet as well and did not allow the opposition to release the pressure. Just when Rizwan and Babar were starting to shift momentum, the spin wizard Rashid Khan nipped out the Pakistan skipper which put a spring in the step for Afghanistan. Despite having Pakistan in a precarious position, Afghanistan were unable to wrap up the innings and Hashmatullah Shahidi will be hoping that it does not come back to haunt them.

A great fightback with the bat from Pakistan and they end up with 268 on the board! After Babar Azam called it right and opted to put runs on the board, Pakistan were off to a sedate start, scoring 34 runs in the first 8 overs. As a result of this start, Fakhar Zaman and Imam-ul-Haq felt the need to get a move on and lost their wickets in the process. Babar Azam and Mohammad Rizwan then joined hands to do a rebuilding job for Pakistan. The duo could not find the fence much but were prepared to grind it out. With 20 overs remaining in the innings, Rizwan in particular upped the ante with a flick of the switch and brought up his fifty, and so did Babar. In no time, Pakistan lost four wickets to be reduced to 189-6. Agha Salman and Mohammad Nawaz joined hands and provided stability to the innings with handy knocks. Salman batted through and propelled his side to 268.

Commentary.Commentary: We are all set for the third ODI to commence. Hot and humid conditions greet the two umpires and the Afghanistan players as they make their way out to the middle. They are joined by the two openers of Pakistan, Fakhar Zaman and Imam-ul-Haq. Fazalhaq Farooqi has the new ball in hand and will start the proceedings with the ball for Afghanistan. Off we go...

PITCH REPORT - HD Ackerman is pitchside and he says that they will be playing on a fresh pitch. Explains that there has been a lot of cricket played on this venue with the emerging Asia Cup and the Lanka Premier League played here. Adds that this pitch has not been used much though so it looks really good. Mentions that it is shorter to one side while the other side is the same as the straight boundary. He is joined by Aamer Sohail who says that it is a much better-looking pitch than the one they have had at Hambantota. Claims that it is very hard with a grass covering which will help the ball slide onto the bat. Ends by saying that the team batting first will be required to get 260 and maybe go beyond that.

Afghanistan skipper Hashmatullah Shahidi says that in the last game, they played some good cricket and they will give their best in this game also. He adds that for 2 years they have been playing really good cricket and qualifying directly for the World Cup is a boost for them. He ends by mentioning the two changes in his team - Gulbadin Naib comes in for Ikram Alikhil and Abdul Rahman makes way for Fareed Ahmad.

Babar Azam, the skipper of Pakistan, says that they will bat first. Adds. that the pitch looks dry with a little bit of grass. Reckons that the first ten overs will be crucial. Also says that they want to put runs on the board and put pressure on Afghanistan. Mentions that they want to win every game they play and want to win the series as well. Informs that there are four changes in the team. Shares that they are pretty satisfied with the performance in the series and want to try different combinations. Feels that this pitch is different than the one used in LPL and reckons that 280-290 will be a good total.

Pakistan (Playing XI) - Fakhar Zaman, Imam-ul-Haq, Babar Azam (C), Mohammad Rizwan (WK), Saud Shakeel (In for Iftikhar Ahmed), Agha Salman, Shadab Khan, Mohammad Nawaz (In for Usama Mir), Faheem Ashraf (In for Naseem Shah), Shaheen Afridi, Mohammad Wasim (In for Haris Rauf).

Afghanistan (Playing XI) - Rahmanullah Gurbaz (WK), Ibrahim Zadran, Hashmatullah Shahidi (C), Gulbadin Naib (In for Ikram Alikhil), Riaz Hassan, Shahidullah Kamal, Mohammad Nabi, Fareed Ahmad (In for Abdul Rahman), Rashid Khan, Mujeeb Ur Rahman, Fazalhaq Farooqi.
TOSS - The coin toss lands in the favour of Pakistan and Babar Azam has opted to BAT first.

Afghanistan, on the other hand, faced an embarrassing defeat in the first ODI where 8 of their batters were dismissed for single-digit scores out of which 4 were sent back to the pavilion for a duck. However, they bounced back in the second ODI where they managed to record their highest ODI total against Pakistan. Their openers Rahmanullah Gurbaz and Ibrahim Zadran made it possible with a massive 227-run partnership between them with Rahmanullah Gurbaz going on to score 151. After the steady opening stand none of the other batters could establish themselves that well. Their bowlers almost clinched the game for them as Fazalhaq Farooqi got 3 wickets and Mohammad Nabi with 2. They had almost won the game if not for some poor fielding efforts in the deep. With the Asia Cup and World Cup right around the corner, both the teams will hope that their squad performs well giving them the necessary boost for the coming tournaments. Will Pakistan whitewash Afghanistan or will Afghanistan end this series on a positive note? We will find out soon as live action will take centre stage shortly. Stay with us as we bring you the toss and team news shortly...

Pakistan has been very dominating in the series clinching the series by winning the first two matches. The first match had been a very easy win for them as they finished off the game in 19.2 overs and gave Pakistan a 142-run win over their opponents. The second match was a very close and interesting encounter as the action went on right till the last over. They just about managed to win by 1 wicket and with 1 ball to spare. Their bowlers performed well towards the end of the innings taking quick wickets and restricting Afghanistan to a score of 300 on a pretty good batting pitch. Their batters however struggled in the middle phase but some meaningful knocks from Imam-ul-Haq, Babar Azam, Shadab Khan, and a quick ending by Naseem Shah pushed them just over the line to victory. In this match, Pakistan will want a clean sweep.
Hello and a very warm welcome folks. We are approaching the third and final ODI of this series between Afghanistan and Pakistan. We arrive at the R Premadasa Stadium in Colombo for this encounter.
... MATCH DAY ...

We arrive at the third and final game in this short three-match ODI series as Afghanistan have toured Sri Lanka to face their subcontinent rivals Pakistan in what has so far been a fiery encounter between the foes. Pakistan have shown dominance in this battle as they have managed to clinch the series having won the first two games and despite this tie being a dead rubber, the Afghans will want to play for their pride. We now move to the R.Premadasa Stadium in Colombo having witnessed the first two matches at the Mahinda Rajapaksa International Stadium in Hambantota and Pakistan will want a clean sweep in the capital city of Sri Lanka. The first game was a one-sided affair and the batters from both sides had an off day with just 260 runs being scored in the game. Having elected to bat first, Pakistan only managed to post 201 runs on the board courtesy of a half-century from Imam-ul-Haq and 30-plus scores from Iftikhar Ahmed and Shadab Khan. It was the spinners who did the damage for Afghanistan claiming 8 wickets between them but their batters failed to deliver as they were bundled out for just 59 runs. Haris Rauf claimed a five-wicket haul as it was the pace bowlers for Pakistan who did the bulk of the damage taking 8 wickets together as well. Afghanistan came back strong with the bat in the second game as their openers put on a 227-run partnership for the first wicket. Rahmanullah Gurbaz scored 151 runs and Ibrahim Zadran made 80 as they helped their team post 300 runs on the board. The Pakistan bowlers lacked the bite in this game with Shaheen Afridi claiming two wickets while Naseem Shah and Usama Mir chipped in with one each. A 30 from Fakhar Zaman and half-centuries from Babar Azam and Imam-ul-Haq who fell short of his hundred by 9 runs, kept Pakistan in the hunt but a collapse through the middle saw them go behind in the game. Shadab Khan proved to be the hero towards the end scoring 48 runs in 35 deliveries and a late cameo from Naseem Shah in the last over helped their side win by one wicket with a ball to spare. Pakistan may look to rotate their squad with the series decided and the Cricket World Cup around the corner but Afghanistan will most likely stick to their playing eleven in the quest for a win. Will Pakistan register a whitewash? Or will Afghanistan get a consolation win? We will find out soon.
